target: visit: the displayed individual visits the advertiser during the campaign period

feature_map.organic_logit: log-odds of the displayed individual's organic (no-ad) probability of visiting the advertiser during the campaign period: in the data the stratum's complier baseline, in the simulator the individual's own organic visit probability (ad_response@2 input organic_visit_probability)

selection.rule: E4: among candidates with compute <= 100 us/row, order by the validation primary metric (ties within 1e-4 to the simpler); keep the first unless its validation long-horizon measure is worse than the smallest one with a paired cluster-bootstrap 95% interval of the difference entirely above 0; keep a simple baseline instead if it is strictly better on test
selection.reason: selected on validation and confirmed on test: no simple baseline is better

bootstrap.kind: Poisson bootstrap of the stratum cells (iid users)

provenance.population: 13,979,592 users reachable by Criteo display advertising (pooled incrementality tests)
provenance.platform: Criteo display advertising (retargeting and prospecting campaigns of undisclosed advertisers)
provenance.identification_label_revision: Label corrected after the fit (2026-11-26, wave-3 repair pass): the plan and the original card said 'randomized_controlled_trial', the design of the data; the kept estimand is a complier (IV) effect of display with randomised eligibility as the instrument, which also rests on the exclusion restriction (identification_note). Nothing was refitted.

limits: Criteo Uplift v2.1 (13,979,592 users of pooled randomised incrementality tests of Criteo display advertising; advertisers, countries and dates undisclosed; released 2018; sub-sampled non-uniformly by the publisher). The simulator may use this model for: the visit probability of an individual who is displayed (and, through ad_response@2, attends) an advertiser's display or feed campaign during a campaign period, as a log-odds shift of that individual's own organic visit probability. It may NOT infer: (1) effects for compliers unlike Criteo's - the displayed users were chosen by Criteo's bidder (exposure rises from about 0.1% to 15% of eligible users with the baseline score), so the effect is that of a targeted display on users a bidder reached; (2) effects of ad content, creative quality, price or relevance (not observed; ad_response@2 adds relevance and repetition only through a separate attention model and a declared assumption); (3) frequency, wear-in, wear-out, carry-over or repeated campaigns (no timestamps, one period per user); (4) negative effects (floored at 0); (5) absolute rates: the publisher's sub-sampling distorts levels; the log-odds shift is invariant to sub-sampling that depends on the outcome or on the arm only, not to sub-sampling that depends on exposure; (6) search advertising (a click on a sponsored result is a different decision). Strata are bins of a pre-treatment score; within-stratum heterogeneity is averaged, and the complier baseline of each stratum is a moment estimate (noisy where exposure is rare; clipped to [1e-4, 0.999]).
name: ad_exposure_response
